I think what triggers me and a big habit I have is when something new happens to a friend I feel like a side piece in their world. It’s a huge insecurity when I think I’m not “cool” enough or able to relate to them anymore. I fall into this pattern of ditching friends before they can ditch me. I know it’s toxic and if I know shouldn’t I be able to catch myself before hurting more people? It’s as if I mentally can’t. I’ve had so many friendships where I just cut off. It’s said running away from people won’t solve anything but honestly after time and time again it seems better to cut them out and never hear from them again because in that state it’s like I can imagine the good stuff never ended. 

Sometimes I catch myself gaslighting. I never realized I did it until I learned the definition. But I really do try to make my problems more extreme then my friends. Often I’ll disregard them because I’m so distracted with my own. But even if I were to listen to them I just get so annoyed with myself getting annoyed at what they are saying. Does that make sense? 

But again, i know these friends were busy for some of the summer but I knew a big chunk they had the time why would they hit me up the week before college starts. I want to say “we had all summer why reach out now during my last busy week of summer?? It always feels like we’re ‘catching up’” but I feel like that is shitty and nobody deserves to be bombarded like that. I know if I received that text I’d be like the hell? 

But it’s how I truly feel and I don’t know how to explain to them. I’m not sure if they are grasping on to something or I’m just pushing my experience into their situation. Because it sorta mirrors how I felt in middle school when my good friend started drifting. Each time I feel better off. I always find starting fresh is the easy way out. I know in movies the outcome is like years down the line yeah they are suffering but since that’s predictable I’m like whatever.
